title: What is this? Three genders
title_target: Τι είναι αυτό; — Tee ee-neh ahf-toh;
goal: Ask for and name objects, use the articles ο / η / το that can't be left out, and accept that every Greek noun has a gender — including tables, the sea, and problems.
bekal: ask "what is this?" and "who is that?"
name objects together with the right article
recognize gender from the ending of the word
use αυτός / αυτή / αυτό to match the noun
use the article in front of people's names

dialogs.title: ΔΙΑΛΟΓΟΣ — At Eleni's apartment
dialogs.intro: Ana is invited to drop by her classmate Eleni's place. Notice that **not a single** noun below stands alone: every one is preceded by ο, η, το, or ένας, μία, ένα.

lines.speaker: Ελένη:
lines.id: Welcome, Ana! This is my home.
lines.literal: well — you-came, Anna! this — it-is — the — house — my.

lines.speaker: Ελένη:
lines.id: It's a cup. And this is the kitchen.
lines.literal: this — it-is — a — cup. and — this (fem.) — it-is — the — kitchen.

lines.speaker: Ελένη:
lines.literal: this (masc.) — he-is — the — Nikos, the — brother — my.

lines.speaker: Νίκος:
lines.literal: health — to-you! you-are — the — friend (fem.) — of — Eleni?

lines.speaker: Άννα:
lines.id: Yes! I'm Ana. Nice to meet you.
lines.literal: yes! I-am — the — Anna. I-rejoice — much.

lines.speaker: Νίκος:
lines.id: The coffee is ready. And the water is cold.
lines.literal: the — coffee — it-is — ready. and — the — water — it-is — cold.

lines.speaker: Άννα:
lines.id: Perfect! One moment — what are those?
lines.literal: perfect! one — minute — what — they-are — these (neut. pl.)?

lines.speaker: Ελένη:
lines.id: Those are my books. I'm a teacher.
lines.literal: these (neut. pl.) — they-are — the (pl.) — books — my. I-am — teacher (fem.).

lines.speaker: Άννα:
lines.literal: very — beautiful! the — Greek — it-is — lovely.

notes: **Every Greek noun has one of three genders, and the article shows which.** ο for masculine, η for feminine, το for neuter. ⚠️ This has nothing to do with living things: **ο καφές** coffee is masculine, **η θάλασσα** the sea is feminine, **το νερό** water is neuter. There's no logic to look for — just three thousand years of habit.

**So always learn a noun together with its article.** Not *σπίτι* but **το σπίτι**. Not *καφές* but **ο καφές**. It's a small habit that saves you months later, when adjectives and articles have to agree too.

⚠️ **The article is also used in front of people's names.** *Είμαι **η** Άννα.* *Αυτός είναι **ο** Νίκος.* To English ears this sounds like "I'm the Anna", but to Greeks it feels warm and everyday, not odd at all. Dropping it actually sounds stiff, like an official announcement.
**Country names take the article too**: **η** Ελλάδα, **η** Ινδονησία, **η** Ιαπωνία, **η** Ιταλία, but **ο** Καναδάς and **τα** Ηνωμένα Έθνη. Most country names happen to be feminine.

**Ένα φλιτζάνι means both "a cup" and "one cup".** Greek uses the number one as its indefinite article, just like French *un/une*. English "a" works the same way, so this one is easy — only remember that it changes with gender.

**Καλώς ήρθες / Καλώς ήρθατε** (*kah-LOHS EER-thehs / EER-thah-teh*) = "welcome", casual and polite. The reply isn't "thank you" but **Καλώς σε βρήκα** / **Καλώς σας βρήκα** — "glad to find you well". This pair sounds very Greek and instantly makes your host smile.

**Ποιος; means "who" and changes with gender**: Ποιος είναι; (a man), Ποια είναι; (a woman), Ποιο είναι; (neuter — here it means "which one"). ⚠️ Don't confuse it with **Πού;** (*poo*), which means "where" — when written fast, they differ by a single letter.

grammars.title: Three genders and their articles
body: This table is the skeleton of the whole Greek language. Everything that comes later — adjectives, pronouns, the object form — leans on it. The good news: the basic table has only six boxes.

head: Masculine (ΑΡΣΕΝΙΚΟ)
Feminine (ΘΗΛΥΚΟ)
Neuter (ΟΥΔΕΤΕΡΟ)
rows: ο καφές, ο δρόμος, ο άντρας
η ώρα, η πόλη, η θάλασσα
το νερό, το παιδί, το πρόβλημα

after: ⚠️ **Masculine and feminine plurals share the same article: οι.** Only the noun ending tells them apart (-οι vs -ες). One less thing to memorize.

The ending is a correct guess about eight times out of ten. The most common traps: **η οδός** (street) is feminine even though it ends in -ος, and **το κορίτσι** (girl) is **neuter** even though it clearly refers to a girl. That last one is no insult — all the little words ending in -ι are neuter, including **το αγόρι** (boy) and **το παιδί** (child).

grammars.title: Αυτός, αυτή, αυτό — a "this" that follows the noun
body: English has one word "this" for everything. Greek picks its form according to the gender of the thing you're pointing at — and that form is exactly the same as the pronoun "he / she / it".

head: Form
Say it
Used for
Example
rows: Αυτός είναι ο Νίκος. — This is Nikos.
Αυτή είναι η Ελένη. — This is Eleni.
neuter things **and** anything not yet identified
Τι είναι αυτό; — What is this?

after: ⚠️ **If you don't know what the thing is yet, use αυτό.** The question *Τι είναι αυτό;* is always neuter, because you can't know the gender before you know the name. Only after the answer does the form adjust: *Αυτή είναι η κουζίνα.*
For a more distant "that", Greek has **εκείνος, εκείνη, εκείνο** (*eh-KEE-nohs*). In everyday conversation αυτός covers both, so don't rush to learn it.

sections.title: The things you'll point at most often

blocks.text: Notice that the first column always includes the article. Cover the English with your finger and try to guess the gender — if you get eight out of twenty right, that's perfectly normal for day two.

blocks.title: Three clues for guessing gender
items: **Ends in -ος, -ας, -ης → almost always masculine.** ο δρόμος, ο άντρας, ο μαθητής. The most common exceptions: η οδός, η μέθοδος, η είσοδος.
**Ends in -α, -η → almost always feminine.** η ώρα, η πόλη, η γυναίκα. Exceptions: ο πατέρας, ο άντρας — both refer to men, so they're easy to remember.

**Ends in -ο, -ι, -μα → neuter, with no exceptions you need right now.** το βιβλίο, το σπίτι, το πρόβλημα. ⚠️ All the loanwords you already know from English — πρόβλημα, σύστημα, πρόγραμμα, θέμα, κλίμα (problem, system, program, theme, climate) — belong to the **-μα** group, and all of them are neuter. That's dozens of free words at once.

Put the words in the right order.
Translate into Greek. Don't forget the article.

answers: Ο — Η — Το — Ο — Το — Η
Τι είναι αυτό; — Αυτός είναι ο Νίκος. — Αυτό είναι το σπίτι μου. — Ο καφές είναι έτοιμος. — Η Ελλάδα είναι όμορφη.
Αυτό είναι το σπίτι μου. — Το νερό είναι κρύο. — Ποιος είναι αυτός; — Είμαι η Άννα. — Η Ελλάδα είναι όμορφη.
